chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the zakat: For what the sky and the rivers irrigate, when it is flowing water or it is unwatered land, the one-tenth is due. And whatever is irrigated by the water-lifting devices and the buckets, or watered by the large water-skin, then half of the one-tenth is due.

key_terms.الدَّوَالِي: plural of daliya — bucket irrigation systems, often using counterweighted poles (shaduf)
key_terms.السَّوَانِي: plural of saniya — animal-drawn water-lifting devices (water wheels driven by camels or oxen)
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: here refers specifically to zakat al-zuru' (agricultural zakat/tithe), not voluntary charity
key_terms.الْعُشْر: one-tenth (10%) — the zakat rate for naturally irrigated crops
key_terms.الْغَرْب: large leather bucket or water-skin used for drawing water from wells
key_terms.بَعْل: unwatered land — crops that draw water from the soil or groundwater without irrigation
key_terms.سَيْح: flowing or gushing water — land irrigated by naturally flowing water such as streams
key_terms.نِصْف الْعُشْر: half of the one-tenth — i.e., 5% — the zakat rate for crops requiring human effort to irrigate

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic zakat rate on crops irrigated by rain vs human effort according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational rule for agricultural zakat (ushr): crops irrigated by natural water sources (rain, rivers, or groundwater) are assessed at a full 10%, while crops requiring human labor for irrigation (water wheels, buckets, or large water-skins) are assessed at only 5%. This differential reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle of reducing the tax burden proportionally to the effort and cost incurred. This ruling is consistent with well-known hadith of the Prophet (SAWW) and was a matter of consensus among classical jurists.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding the charity in what the sky and the rivers irrigate when it was arid or it was un-watered, is the one-tenth, and whatever is irrigated by the scoops and the buckets, or irrigated by the human energy, so it is half of the one-tenth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Zakat on what is watered by canals or rain from the sky, is one out of ten and on what is watered by means of scoops and buckets and what trickles thereby is one out of twenty.’”
